title: H202-variant: bias correction mask adds 0.44 Sharpe-point to ML momentum — test on our universe
rationale: arXiv:2507.07107 (2025) found that bias elimination is the first-order performance driver for ML-enhanced cross-sectional momentum — contributing a 0.44 Sharpe-point improvement exceeding any model architecture choice. The paper uses a 'mask' to prevent look-ahead bias in training. Our H198 momentum uses simple signal lookback (6-1m) which should be clean, but we haven't tested ML-enhanced signal selection. A new hypothesis could test whether an XGBoost/LightGBM signal selector (trained on IS data with bias mask) outperforms the simple 6-1m return rank on our 30-stock OOS universe.
content:
# H202 — ML-Enhanced Cross-Sectional Momentum with Bias Correction
# Based on arXiv:2507.07107: bias elimination mask adds 0.44 Sharpe-point
# Test: XGBoost signal selector vs simple 6-1m return rank (H198 baseline)
# Universe: same 30-stock S&P 500 universe as H198
# Features: 9 Alpha101-derived factors including momentum, volume-intraday corr, open-volume divergence
# IS: 2013-2020, OOS: 2021-2026
# Confirm: OOS Sharpe > H198 baseline (1.174), Cumul > 1.3x
# NOTE: requires proper bias mask — train only on IS data, strict temporal cutoff
